![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/37674375730f32a70d7909a7ab01f3f9c836cf9c72d16447d499af20427f022c.png)

For a random variable $Z∼N(0,1)$ we have the following symmetry property for $a>0:$

$$
P(Z>-a)=P(Z<a)=Φ(a)
$$

We're given that $Z∼N(0,1),$ and we wish to compute $P(Z>-1.43).$ The required probability is represented by the area shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/c80581cf6e8c2662626f70b27b669233a7bed35637dc16771c9b4a1162830efc.png)

By symmetry, this equals the area corresponding to the probability $P(Z<1.43).$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/capture/differential/14259374/assets/014dd9aa3e4b021ae940cb6bf4fc631cb59a88ad36978ae6d152cceae41256bd.png)

Therefore,

$$
P(Z>-1.43)=P(Z<1.43)=Φ(1.43)=0.9236.
$$
